lines.japanese: 「隼人さーん！　お茶買っていきましょう、お茶！　あの水筒型になってるやつ買いましょう！」
lines.english: “Hayato! Let’s buy tea for the trip! Let’s get the kind that comes in those canteen-shaped bottles!”

lines.japanese: 「おう」
lines.english: “Sure.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、雑誌もあった方がいいですかねー？　あとお菓子ー」
lines.english: “Oh, should we buy magazines too? And snacks!”

lines.japanese: 「好きなもん買えって。でも荷物になるようなもん増やすなよ」
lines.english: “Get whatever you want. Just don’t buy so much crap that it turns into a ton of luggage.”

lines.japanese: 「はー、ていうか隼人さん、荷物ほとんどないじゃないですかー。二泊ですよー、平気ですかー？　石鹸とかシャンプーとか持ってきてますー？」
lines.english: “Speaking of luggage, you hardly brought anything, Hayato. We’re staying two nights. Are you sure you’ll be okay? Did you bring soap and shampoo?”

lines.japanese: 「いや俺、でけえ鞄とか持ちたくねンだよ。つかシャンプーとかって、旅館に全部置いてあんじゃないの」
lines.english: “I hate carryin’ big bags. Besides, won’t the inn have stuff like shampoo?”

lines.japanese: 「まー、たぶんアメニティは備わってると思いますけどー。作業着はないですよー？　途中で買っていきますー？」
lines.english: “Well, they probably provide toiletries. But they won’t have work clothes. Should we buy some on the way?”

lines.japanese: 「他の荷物ガン無視で作業着かよ。普通にいらねえだろ、俺らなにしに行くんだよ」
lines.english: “You skip all the other luggage and go straight to work clothes? We obviously don’t need ’em. What do you think we’re going there to do?”

lines.japanese: 「はいー、湯けむり慕情ふたり旅ですねー、げへえ」
lines.english: “For our steamy, wistful lovers’ getaway. Geh-heh.”

lines.japanese: 「うわ、それを分かった上での作業着かよ」
lines.english: “You knew that and still figured I’d need work clothes?”

lines.japanese: 鳴はのっけからテンションが高かった。
lines.english: Naru was excited from the very beginning.

lines.japanese: とはいえ、俺だって充分に浮かれていた。調子に乗って、途中駅で二回も駅弁を買った。
lines.english: Not that I was any better. I got carried away and bought boxed station lunches twice at stations along the way.

lines.japanese: 今日から俺たちは、二泊三日の温泉旅行だ。
lines.english: Starting today, we were taking a three-day, two-night hot-spring trip.

lines.japanese: 目的地は西の彼方、プラチナの実家がある温泉街。
lines.english: Our destination lay far to the west: the hot-spring town where Platinum’s family lived.

lines.japanese: 先日、エージからの依頼でヤバい橋を渡った結果、やつは律儀にも報酬を振りこんできた。
lines.english: Not long ago, I’d taken some serious risks on a job for Eiji. True to his word, he paid me for it.

lines.japanese: 俺はその金で、まず旅行雑誌を買った。
lines.english: The first thing I bought with that money was a travel magazine.

lines.japanese: 次に、それを見ながらうんうん唸って、乗車券と旅館の準備をした。
lines.english: Then I pored over it, groaning and grumbling, and arranged our train tickets and the inn.

lines.japanese: 選び方の基準もよく分からないし、何から何まで人生で初めての経験だったから、俺は相当苦戦させられた。
lines.english: I didn’t even understand how I was supposed to choose. Every part of the process was a first for me, and I had one hell of a time with it.

lines.japanese: それでも窓口の駅員や旅館のおばちゃんと話しながら、なんとか無事に手配することが出来た。
lines.english: Still, after talking things through with the ticket clerk and the lady at the inn, I somehow managed to make all the arrangements.

lines.japanese: ふたりで選ぶのも楽しそうではあったが、いつも何かと世話を焼かせてるツレに、たまにはサプライズってやつをプレゼントしてやりたかったんだ。
lines.english: Choosing together would’ve been fun too, but for once, I wanted to surprise the girl who was always taking care of me.

lines.japanese: あらかじめ予定を確認しておいた三連休。ちょっと付きあってくれ、とか言ってチケットを渡すと、やつは目をまん丸にして、しばらく返事もしなかった。
lines.english: I’d checked her schedule ahead of time for the three-day weekend. When I said I wanted her to come somewhere with me and handed over the tickets, her eyes went round and she didn’t answer for a while.

lines.japanese: 「ふっ、ふわああァーッ！！」
lines.english: “Fw-fwaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: そして返事より先に、謎の音を発した。
lines.english: Then, before answering, she made a mysterious noise.

lines.japanese: アタマの良いこいつでも、一瞬では整理しきれないほどのサプライズだったらしい。
lines.english: Apparently the surprise was too much for even someone as smart as her to process at once.

lines.japanese: それなら俺も嬉しい。
lines.english: That made me happy too.

lines.japanese: 「あっ、あり、あり……あり？　ありがっ……」
lines.english: “Th-tha, tha... thank...!”

lines.japanese: 「おう。まあ？　俺も行ってみたかったし？　つって、鳴も行きたいんなら、丁度いいかなと思って」
lines.english: “Yeah. I mean, I wanted to go too, y’know? And I figured if you wanted to go, then it worked out for both of us.”

lines.japanese: 「えっ、あのっ、でもっ……あの、お金……」
lines.english: “B-but, um... what about the money...?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、平気。まっとうに働いてたら、ボーナスが入った」
lines.english: “Don’t worry. I did an honest job and got a bonus.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ家族や小鳩はさ、いずれ別の形で連れてってやろうと思ってる。でもまずは、今まで大したことしてやれなかった鳴に？　みたいなこと考えちゃって──」
lines.english: “I’ll take the family and Kobato somewhere else another time. But first, I thought maybe I should do something for you, since I haven’t done much for you yet—”

lines.japanese: 「――まあいいや、なんか説明しても上手く伝わんねーだろうし。とにかくあれだ、一緒いけば分かるから」
lines.english: “—Ah, forget it. I’m no good at explaining, and I won’t get it across anyway. Just... you’ll understand when we go together.”

lines.japanese: 俺は照れ隠しに、後ろ頭をがしがし掻きながらそっぽを向いた。
lines.english: Trying to hide my embarrassment, I vigorously scratched the back of my head and looked away.

lines.japanese: 「うっ」
そしたら、目の前から何かを飲みこむような音が聞こえてきた。
lines.english: Then I heard a sound from in front of me, like someone swallowing something.

lines.japanese: 「ううっ……」
lines.english: “Uuugh...”

lines.japanese: 振りむけば、やつの目の端に光るものがあった。
lines.english: When I turned back, tears glimmered in the corners of her eyes.

lines.japanese: 「え、なにこれ……俺？　え、俺？」
lines.english: “What? Is this... me? Did I do this?”

lines.japanese: 「ううっ、ひっく、ううええっ……」
lines.english: “Uuugh, hic, uwaaah...”

lines.japanese: 「えええーっ。な、なんで泣いてんのおまえ」
lines.english: “Whaaat? Wh-why are you crying?”

lines.japanese: 「だっ、だって嬉しいじゃないでずがっ」
lines.english: “B-because I’m so happyyyy!”

lines.japanese: 「ぶええ――っ！」
lines.english: “Bwaaaaaah!”

lines.japanese: 「ちょ、おまえそのまま抱きつくんじゃねえよ。鼻ふけ鼻」
lines.english: “Hey, don’t hug me like that. Blow your nose first.”
